title: TextEvaluationAndRevisionSchema
description: Evaluates a written text for readability, rhetorical stance, sentence variety, and academic vocabulary based on classical and modern rhetorical frameworks, providing actionable revision suggestions.

current_grade_band.description: The estimated educational grade band of the analyzed text.

target_grade_band.description: The desired target audience grade band.

flesch_kincaid_grade_level.description: The mathematically calculated Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level.

conceptual_accessibility_summary.description: Qualitative assessment of how well complex concepts are scaffolded for the target audience without dilution.

is_established.description: True if the text frames its argument within an existing conversation or counter-view ('They Say') before asserting its own thesis.

summary_of_context.description: A description of the consensus, assumption, or counter-view being addressed.

strength_assessment.description: Critique of how effectively this context motivates and justifies the author's intervention.

stance_type.description: The primary rhetorical positioning relative to the 'They Say'.

is_present.description: True if a preemptive naysayer or skeptic's objection is integrated into the text.

skeptic_group_identified.description: The specific group or perspective of skeptics referenced (e.g., 'traditionalists', 'critics').

objection_handling_critique.description: An analysis of how successfully the text dismantles or responds to the skeptic's objection.

concession_rebuttal_pivots.description: Identified points of nuanced disagreement, agreement-with-concession, or qualification.

concession_text.description: The portion of the text conceding a minor point or validating the counter-argument.

rebuttal_text.description: The portion of the text that pivots back to defend the primary claim.

template_alignment.description: Alignment with templates like 'Yes, but...', 'Although I concede X, I still insist Y'.

genre_moves.description: Structural moves identified based on John Swales' Genre Analysis (e.g., Establishing a Territory, Establishing a Niche, Occupying the Niche).

move_name.description: The name of the move (e.g., Move 1: Establishing a territory, Move 2: Creating a research space, Move 3: Introducing present research).

text_segment.description: The specific excerpt of text representing this move.

rhetorical_purpose.description: How this move advances the communicative purpose within the discourse community.

variety_critique.description: Critique of sentence rhythm, length variation, and stylistic impact of sentence structures.

nominalization_density.description: Frequency of verbs turned into nouns (e.g., 'analysis' instead of 'analyze') which abstracts agency.

stylistic_appropriateness.description: Evaluation of whether voice shifts are strategically deployed (e.g., passive voice for a formal scientific register, active voice for vivid accountability).

given_new_alignment.description: Adherence to the 'Given-New' cohesion contract where sentences begin with known information and end with new focal points.

cohesive_ties_critique.description: Analysis of transitions, repetition of key concepts, and structural links between sentences and paragraphs.

tier_1.description: Count of everyday, basic vocabulary terms.

tier_2.description: Count of high-frequency general academic vocabulary (e.g., evaluate, formulate).

tier_3.description: Count of domain-specific, low-frequency technical terms (e.g., photosynthesis, subduction).

tier_2_words_identified.description: Key Tier 2 academic words observed in the text.

tier_3_words_identified.description: Key Tier 3 specialized terms observed in the text.

recoding_opportunities.description: Suggestions where academic terms can be temporarily 'recoded' (translated) to improve conceptual grasp without losing the formal vocabulary itself.

suggested_informal_bridge.description: A student-friendly synonym, metaphor, or analogy.

pedagogical_rationale.description: Why this recoding maintains rigor while ensuring cognitive accessibility.

actionable_revisions.description: Highly specific recommendations for altering the text's tone, register, or authority.

original_text_segment.description: The verbatim text segment slated for modification.

focus_area.description: The primary dimension of the text being improved.

theoretical_framework.description: The specific source framework that justifies this change.

concise_rationale.description: A crisp, professional explanation linking the syntactic/structural edit directly to its rhetorical effect on tone, register, or authority.
